title: Arne Slot says he is confident of remaining Liverpool coach beyond season
content:
Arne Slot believes he will keep his job as Liverpool head coach this summer.

The Dutch head coach has found himself under mounting pressure during a turbulent season for the defending Premier League champions.

Liverpool have lost 18 games in all competitions and remain in a battle to secure Champions League qualification with two matches remaining. Boos greeted the final whistle of last Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Chelsea at Anfield, but the 47-year-old former Feyenoord boss retains the support of the club’s hierarchy.

Asked if he expects to remain in charge for next season, Slot said: “I don’t think I am deciding that alone by myself, but I have every reason to believe I am the Liverpool manager next season.

“First of all, I am contracted to this club (until 2027) and second of all from all the talks we are having. That is my take on it.

“But if you don’t have the best season, especially if you compare with last season — if you compare it with other seasons you might have a different debate — this has definitely not been a great season, then it is also normal that criticism comes.

“We have all had our share, and with ‘all’ I mean the players have had their share, the managerand other people in the club. That is how things work nowadays if you don’t win the league.”

A growing number of supporters have been demanding change, but Slot has been heavily involved in formulating the club’s pre-season schedule and summer recruitment plans.

“If a manager or a club doesn’t have their best season there is always a debate — that is the new reality in football,” he added.

“It is not up to me to judge the people who judge me. They have every right to have their opinion and in this modern time everyone can share his opinion as well.”

Slot said: “We know where we go on tour (to the U.S.) so our plans have been made and talks have been ongoing between the club and new players and I am involved in that.”

Mohamed Salah and Alisson have both returned to training ahead of Friday’s Premier League trip to Aston Villa with Liverpool knowing that victory will secure Champions League football.

Ibrahima Konate is also fit after coming off against Chelsea last weekend, while Florian Wirtz is battling to overcome illness.

“Ibou is okay, he trained with us,” Slot said. “Mo will be available tomorrow for only a few minutes, but hopefully he can come in. Alisson trains with us again, let’s see where he is tomorrow, if he is ready or has to wait one more week.

“Flo had a stomach infection, so let’s see how fit he is. He’s on antibiotics.”

Liverpool’s fanbase is restless.

The dissent shown towards Slot during the game against Chelsea at Anfield underlined how patience is in short supply.

It’s not just poor results which have triggered a torrent of criticism but the uninspiring brand of football which has failed to engage and excite supporters this season.

Many have been demanding change with calls for Xabi Alonso to replace Slot as head coach growing louder. However, The Athletic have reported that Slot retains the backing of the club’s owners and Slot’s latest response to questions about his future only reinforced that stance.

Based on his conversations with Michael Edwards, Fenway Sports Group’s CEO of football, and sporting director Richard Hughes, Slot clearly expects to be given the opportunity to put right what’s gone wrong this season.

Rather than fretting about the outcome of a possible end of season review, Slot is focused on pre-season plans and summer transfer targets. He spoke like someone who had clarity regarding his future and it would now require a major U-turn for him to depart this summer.

Edwards and Hughes believe there are mitigating factors for Liverpool’s woes – from the tragic loss of Diogo Jota last July to the injury crisis, new signings needing time to adapt to the demands of the Premier League and established stars losing their way.

Slot still has credit in the bank with the hierarchy after last season’s title triumph but he faces a real battle to try to win back the support of those fans who have turned against him.
